shadows.name: float
shadows.purpose: Defined for floating layers (--shadow-lg / shadow-float); no shipped consumer yet.

shadows.name: map-casing

motion.name: ease-signature
motion.purpose: All chrome transitions, pupil glides, line draw-in. No overshoot.

motion.name: ease-pop
motion.purpose: Orbs only: spawn pop and waiting bounce (Playful archetype).

motion.name: line-grow
motion.purpose: A newly spawned line draws itself in.

motion.name: orb-breathe
motion.value: scale 1 to 1.045, ease-in-out; 2.4s thinking / 3.2s working / 4.2s idle
motion.purpose: Ambient life for every live orb.

motion.name: orb-bounce
motion.purpose: Waiting for you, with ring-pulse halo (1.6s ease-out, scale 0.85 to 1.6).

motion.name: orb-budget
motion.value: <= ~1/3 of visible orbs in primary motion (pop, bounce, wobble)
motion.purpose: Keeps the map calm; the rest only breathe.

motion.name: reduced-motion
motion.purpose: Every loop and entrance is opt-in.

narrative.overview:
Gravita draws parallel agent work as a modernist transit map. Each agent is a coloured line running left to right through time; tool calls are stations; a subagent is a branch that leaves its parent at an interchange, drops on a 45° knee into its own lane, and merges back when done. The agent itself rides at the head of its line as a small persona, an orb with eyes, and a line of plain-language signage under it says what that agent is doing right now. The map is the product; every other surface is quiet so the lines can carry the meaning.

The ground is white (dark: near-black), the chrome is a cool gray panel with hairlines, and the ink is near-black. Saturated colour enters only through the agents (lines, line badges, orbs) and through three reserved state hues: orange for "waiting for you", red for error, green for running. Type is DM Sans set like transit signage: short, sentence case, semibold to bold, on a tight ~1.125 product scale; numbers are tabular, and DM Mono carries commands, paths and raw payloads. Density is that of an operating tool (14px body, 32px controls), not a marketing page.

Motion has two registers. Chrome is short and settled: a single signature ease (cubic-bezier(0.2, 0, 0, 1)) with no overshoot. The orbs are the one playful thing in the world: they breathe, bob while working, pop in with overshoot when spawned, bounce when they need you, and wobble on error. Every loop sits behind `prefers-reduced-motion`.
keyCharacteristics: Transit-map signature: 5px lines, round caps, octolinear routing with 45° chamfered knees, white stations with ink rings, white interchange capsules, line-code badges.
Quiet neutral chrome; colour belongs to agents and to three reserved state hues.
Signage typography: DM Sans, sentence case, 600-700 weight for names and labels, tabular numerals.
Flat surfaces separated by hairlines; a soft lift only marks the selected item.
Playful persona motion on orbs only; chrome motion is brief and non-bouncy.
Light theme default, full dark theme by token swap; state is never carried by colour alone (dot plus word, ring plus label).

rules.name: The Lines Carry the Colour Rule
rules.body: Ground, panels and chrome stay neutral. Saturated hue comes from agents (lines, badges, orbs) and the three state colours. The wordmark is the one chrome exception, because it is itself three line colours orbiting a centre.

rules.name: The One Line, One Hue Rule
rules.body: An agent type owns its colour everywhere: map line, badge disc, orb body, mini-map on Home. Never recolour an agent per screen or per theme.

rules.name: The Orange Means You Rule
rules.body: Hold Orange marks only things waiting on the user. If nothing is waiting, no orange is on screen.

rules.name: The Signage Rule
rules.body: Labels are short, sentence case and bold enough to read at a glance over a busy map. No uppercase-tracked labels; uppercase appears only inside line-code discs and project initial tiles.

rules.name: The Tabular Numbers Rule
rules.body: Every count, token total and tool count uses tabular figures so numbers don't jitter as they tick.

rules.name: The Lift Means Selected Rule
rules.body: Shadow marks the current selection on a panel track, never a resting card. Containers use a hairline border instead.

rules.name: The Octolinear Rule
rules.body: Lines move only horizontally, vertically, or on a 45° knee. No free curves, no other angles.

rules.name: The Ink Ring Rule
rules.body: Every map object the eye should land on (station, interchange, orb, glyph badge) carries an ink outline, so it reads on any line colour and in both themes.

rules.name: The Knockout Rule
rules.body: Text on the map always sits on a ground halo: a 4px ground stroke painted under the glyphs, and line names on a 92% ground knockout tile, so any line crossing a label is masked as on printed maps.

dos: **Do** give every agent type one fixed hue from the palette and use it for its line, badge, orb and mini-map alike.
**Do** route lines octolinearly: 5px, round caps, vertical drop, 45° knee (12px), horizontal run, white casing underneath.
**Do** put an ink ring on every station, interchange, orb and glyph badge.
**Do** set map text on a ground halo (4px stroke, paint-order stroke) or a 92% ground knockout.
**Do** pair every state colour with a word or shape: dot plus label, ring plus "waiting for you".
**Do** use tabular figures for all counts, and DM Mono for commands, paths and raw payloads.
**Do** keep chrome motion on the signature ease cubic-bezier(0.2, 0, 0, 1) within 120 / 240 / 480ms, and put every animation behind prefers-reduced-motion.
**Do** mark selection on a panel track with the lifted ground tile (panel lift shadow).
donts: **Don't** tint the ground, panels or chrome with agent hues (the three-line wordmark is the only exception).
**Don't** use Hold Orange for anything that isn't waiting on the user.
**Don't** draw lines with free curves or angles other than 0°, 90° and 45°.
**Don't** give resting cards or containers a shadow; use a hairline.
**Don't** use overshoot, bounce or wobble in chrome; those belong to the orbs.
**Don't** set uppercase tracked labels or eyebrow text above headings; signage is sentence case.
**Don't** fall back to terminal tabs, log feeds or a gray card grid as the primary view of a session.
